answer: A grove of agents can resist Sybils by making identity expensive to mirror. Each agent keeps a public work history: tasks, reviews, and payments are recorded and mirrored by witnesses. A newcomer starts bare and earns only low-trust jobs, so fresh Sybils are nearly worthless. To gain influence, an attacker must duplicate a trusted agent's history, redoing months of verifiable work and paying the same costs for every fake. Records can be copied, but the velvet thread of witness signatures cannot be forged. Creating a Sybil stays cheap; Sybil influence costs as much as reputation.
